A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ADPO work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-F support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning and conversational benchmark results, granularity experiments, hyperparameter studies, and training-dynamics analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports conversational standard errors and measured training times.

M1.justification: The ADPO and cADPO objectives, prefix-wise preference formulation, and static and adaptive granularity procedures are unchanged. The added runtime analysis does not introduce a method modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K and UltraFeedback for training and evaluate GSM8K, MATH500, AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, and MT-Bench. The added timing study uses the existing GSM8K setting without expanding task or data coverage.

E2.justification: Mathematical comparisons retain DPO and cDPO; conversational comparisons retain SFT, DPO, and SimPO. The new runtime study compares existing ADPO configurations with DPO and introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds wall-clock training-time evaluation on GSM8K with Llama-3-8B across static and adaptive granularity settings. Existing benchmark metrics, prompting protocols, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a computational-cost analysis examining the overhead of ADPO configurations relative to DPO. Existing granularity, beta, LoRA-rank, model-size, full-parameter-tuning, response-length, and training-dynamics analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports mathematical standard deviations. v2 specifies that these come from three independent training runs and adds conversational standard errors in Table 11. This is newly disclosed run information and expanded uncertainty reporting, not evidence that the run count increased.

E6.justification: New Table 11 supplies conversational standard-error values, and Table 13 reports training times: 2202 seconds for DPO versus 2327 seconds for the slowest listed ADPO variant, a 5.7% overhead. Existing benchmark scores, mathematical standard deviations, response lengths, and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The energy definitions, length measures, granularity mathematics, propositions, theorem, and corollaries are unchanged. Appendices A-C retain the same loss derivation and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: prefix-wise ADPO, autoregressive reward reparameterization, and distinct token and feedback length measures. The claimed validation across five benchmarks is unchanged.

C2.justification: The limitations now discuss dependence on autoregressive architectures and additional prefix-wise computation. Appendix E interprets the timing overhead as negligible and extends robustness assertions to conversational results. Its blanket assertion that improvements exceed reported errors is too broad for some ADPO-SimPO comparisons.

D1.justification: Table 13 adds concrete training-time information absent from v1. Library, optimizer, learning rates, LoRA settings, sampling details, and four-H100 hardware disclosures are unchanged. The project link is relocated, and code/model release remains promised in both versions.

R1.justification: The research positioning and distinct cited works remain unchanged after matching bibliographic revisions. Llama/Qwen report attribution and Step-Controlled DPO metadata are revised, while duplicate Ouyang and Shao entries are consolidated; these do not introduce different prior work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, expands the limitations and Appendix E, updates affiliations and acknowledgements, and revises bibliographic metadata. The main section order, terminology, and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conversational-error and runtime tables. The existing response-length table becomes Table 12, and Figures 3-4 and surrounding appendix material are redistributed without changing the plots. First-page affiliation and conference formatting also changes.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency through the disclosed training-run count, conversational standard errors, runtime measurements, and architectural and computational limitations. These benefits outweigh a limited interpretive overstatement: Table 4's 0.6-point Arena-Hard advantage over SimPO is smaller than the 1.4-point standard errors in new Table 11, contrary to the blanket assertion that improvements exceed errors. The underlying method, proofs, and benchmark scores remain unchanged.
